faq.question: How does Tirzepatide differ from Semaglutide mechanistically?
faq.answer: Semaglutide activates only GLP-1R. Tirzepatide activates both GIPR and GLP-1R — the GIP component adds insulinotropic effects, improved lipid handling, and better insulin sensitivity. Read the full comparison in our GLP-1 Buyer's Guide →

faq.question: Why is Tirzepatide more expensive than Semaglutide?
faq.answer: Three factors: longer sequence (39 vs 31 AA → more coupling steps, higher material costs), more challenging purification, and higher demand relative to capacity (Tirzepatide is in 'differentiation' phase with growing demand).

faq.question: What salt form is your Tirzepatide?
faq.answer: Standard is the acetate salt. If your protocol requires Na, TFA, or another counterion, specify in your inquiry — salt form can be adjusted during the final purification/lyophilization stage.

faq.question: How do you confirm the identity — not just purity — of Tirzepatide?
faq.answer: Every batch undergoes both HPLC (purity, ≥99% peak area) AND ESI-MS (identity, confirming MW ~4,813.5 Da). For bulk orders: linker integrity by HPLC-ELSD or LC-MS/MS to confirm intact C20 fatty diacid conjugation.
